shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses carry the same friend-root רע in the mercenary-friendship theme: 19:6 closes וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן “everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts” (web:Prov.19.6), and 19:7 opens its second colon with מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ “his friends avoid him” (web:Prov.19.7) — the same root turned from the flatterer's calculus (v.6) to the poor man's abandonment by that same class of "friend" (v.7), a deliberate two-verse elaboration of one social observation rather than two unrelated maxims. 19:7 also carries a ketiv/qere pair at its closing word (לא/לוֹ); a paseq mark sits in the same verse. (oshb:Prov.19.6; oshb:Prov.19.7)
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 19:6 and 19:7 as independent is rejected because 19:7's opening colon ("all the relatives of the poor shun him") completes the a-fortiori logic 19:6 sets up — if everyone chases the gift-giver, how much more do even kin flee the poor; the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6.

queue_items.claim: device_notes calls both cross-seam verbs third-person jussive wishes about the parents' joy; 23:24 is an indicative infinitive-absolute construction and the row's own rationale calls it a general maxim.

queue_items.claim: The stated reason for the medium_low band is an unanchored corpus-wide claim about the book's other headers that the bytes refute.
queue_items.grounds: device_notes asserts that a 'free-standing header verse' is 'the pattern the book's other headers follow elsewhere', with no verse anchors and no digit. Re-derived from the header spine (prov_device_inventory: mishle verse-initial at 1:1 and 10:1; gam-elleh at 24:23 and 25:1; divrei at 30:1 and 31:1; divrei-hakhamim at 1:6 and 22:17): 10:1 carries מִשְׁלֵ֗י שְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה followed by the complete proverb בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם יְשַׂמַּח אָ֑ב וּבֵ֥ן כְּ֝סִ֗יל תּוּגַ֥ת אִמּֽוֹ in the same verse - the identical header-plus-maxim shape the row treats as anomalous at 24:23 - and 22:17 carries דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים mid-verse. The generalization is therefore false precisely where it is load-bearing, and it is stated in corpus register without verse anchors (E-18 arm).
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (device_notes plus confidence): drop the generalization or replace it with the verse-anchored true fact that 10:1 carries the same header-plus-maxim shape, and re-band the boundary decision upward - routed onward for adjudication, not applied.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The band is held on a corpus-wide generalization the book's own bytes refute, so the low label masks a defective warrant rather than recording honest uncertainty. device_notes: 'Confidence is held at medium_low because the three-verse reading rests on treating 24:23's heading-maxim as joined to its own illustration and resolution rather than as a free-standing header verse, the pattern the book's other headers follow elsewhere.' Bytes: the closest structural analogue, 10:1, does exactly what 24:23 does - the header clause מִשְׁלֵ֗י שְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה is followed IN THE SAME VERSE by a complete antithetic proverb בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם יְשַׂמַּח אָ֑ב וּבֵ֥ן כְּ֝סִ֗יל תּוּגַ֥ת אִמּֽוֹ; and the divrei-hakhamim seam at 22:17 stands mid-verse inside its own imperative clause (דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים, tokens 3-4 of 7). Only 1:1, 25:1, 30:1 and 31:1 are header-only verses, and none of them carries an independent maxim that could have been joined to anything. The seam is otherwise well-warranted: גַּם אֵ֥לֶּה is verse-initial (prov_device_inventory: gam-elleh verse-initial at 24:23 and 25:1), and pmarks_Prov.json marks Prov.24.22 = SAMEKH, correctly typed and single-witness-disclosed as corroboration rather than driver. An unnamed inclusio further supports the three-verse span - verse-final טֽוֹב at 24:23 against verse-final בִרְכַּת at 24:25, where verse-final twb occurs in only 12 of 915 Prov verses (2:9, 13:21, 14:14, 14:22, 15:23, 16:29, 19:8, 20:23, 22:1, 24:23, 24:25, 28:10), of which 24:23/24:25 is the only pair within five verses. Confidence reads under-stated on a false reason.

queue_items.claim: The 25:8 to 25:9 seam carries a byte-true legal-dispute catchword this row never discloses, and the row rejects the 25:8-9 cluster on a 'too pervasive' threshold it applies inconsistently with its own neighbouring cluster rows.
queue_items.grounds: Byte facts at the row's right seam: 25:8 and 25:9 share 2 exact skeleton tokens (reekha plus the negative particle, the particle being pervasive at 78 verses book-wide and carrying nothing), and beyond the token the root r-y-b straddles the seam, לָרִ֗ב (oshb:Prov.25.8), word-bound at exactly 1 verse book-wide, against רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב (oshb:Prov.25.9), the two verses being one lawsuit scene. The 25:9 row discloses that same root link at the same seam; this row discloses only reekha, so the standing cross-seam cohesion rule (a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed) is met asymmetrically.
